《Sir Loot-a-Lot》 is a medieval turn-based looter RPG. You play as a lone black-iron knight, venturing deep into goblin lairs, skeletal graveyards, and web-choked abysses. Cut a path through them with sword, spear, and hunting bow, carry every piece of loot back to town, and forge yourself into someone capable of surviving the next expedition.

But combat works a little differently here: your skills are not buttons lined up on a hotbar, waiting for their cooldowns to end. Instead, they are dealt into your hand as cards at the start of every turn.

[h2]When Skills Become Cards, Every Move Becomes a Choice[/h2]

Each turn, the skills you have learned are shuffled back into your hand. You have 4 Action Points and a random set of possibilities to work with.

Quick Slash, Heavy Thrust, Whirlwind Arrow, Poison Coating, Iron Wall, Defensive Counter—what you play, the order you play it in, and where you spend those 4 points turn every round into a small tactical puzzle. You cannot simply repeat the same rotation, because every hand is different.

This is not a traditional card game. There is no complicated deckbuilding and no thick rulebook to study. The cards are simply your skills—only now, they force you to make meaningful choices.

[h2]Sword, Spear, and Hunting Bow: One Knight, Three Fighting Styles[/h2]

You carry three weapons and automatically switch to the appropriate stance whenever you play a card. Close-range slashes, mid-range thrusts, and long-range arrows can flow seamlessly into one another within the same turn.

Some skills reward you for constantly switching stances. Others encourage you to commit to a single weapon and keep attacking. Certain enemies may even begin to recognize—and punish—your habits.

[h2]Poison, Fire, Frost, and the Thrill of Combos[/h2]

Coat your next attack in poison, flame, or frost, causing enemies to bleed, burn, or freeze during their own turns. Chain duplicate cards together with Multi-Slash to unleash an entire sequence of attacks.

Recognize an opportunity that exists for only a single turn, then use it to wipe out an entire group of enemies at once.

[h2]Relics That Give Every Run Its Own Identity[/h2]

The relics you find are not merely another collection of percentage bonuses. They change the way you play.

One might make the first strike of every turn exceptionally deadly. Another may cause an elemental enchantment to last for the entire round. Some may even grant you an additional turn.

Once you assemble two or three relics, your build begins to take shape—and your next expedition may play completely differently.

[h2]Loot Is the True Long-Term Progression[/h2]

Every descent is an expedition. Branching paths lead to regular battles, elite ambushes, blessing chambers, treasure vaults, mysterious merchants, and a boss waiting at the end.

Weapons and armour wear down in battle, but new equipment can also be taken from fallen enemies. Every item you bring back to town remains in your collection, helping you travel a little farther next time.

Relics and temporarily learned skills disappear when an expedition ends. Your equipment collection does not.

[h2]Bosses That Fight Back Intelligently[/h2]

The goblins, undead, and spider swarms each have their own leaders—and they are more than ordinary enemies with larger health bars.

They summon reinforcements, adapt to your fighting style, and place unwanted cards into your hand. Defeating them requires changing your rhythm, not simply attacking more times.

[list]
[] Turn-based card combat where skills become cards and a new hand is dealt every turn
[] Seamlessly combine sword, spear, and hunting-bow stances
[] Poison, fire, and frost enchantments, plus multi-hit combo attacks
[] Run-defining relics that change how you play
[] Equipment drops, durability, crafting, and long-term loot progression
[] Branching expeditions across multiple regions with escalating difficulty
[*] A grim medieval art style and mechanically distinct boss battles
[/list]

Failure does not leave you with nothing.

Return to town. Repair your sword. Then descend once more.

Perdition Flats, Arizona Territory, 1889. You buried them all. You know every name, because you wrote them down. They are not staying buried.

SIX CHAMBERS, AND THEY FIRE IN ORDER

Every level you engrave one chamber. Chamber three bursts, chamber five ricochets, chamber one drinks the blood back. The order never changes, so the cylinder becomes a sequence you read as it turns — and the reload is where you live or die.

There is no screen-clearing light show at minute fifteen. The ceiling is low on purpose. You aim every shot from the first night to the last.

CLOSE IT WITH A FLICK

The cylinder turns as a ring around you, in the middle of the picture where your eyes already are. A bright notch comes round once. Snap it shut with a flick of the mouse, a click, or the spacebar — hit the notch and it closes early, miss it and you are standing in the open with an empty gun.

MARKS THAT TOUCH PAY LIKE A HAND

Put the same mark on neighbouring chambers and they pay out like a poker hand — a pair, three of a kind, a flush across all six. And the cylinder wraps, so chamber six touches chamber one. The bench draws a bracket under exactly the chambers making each hand, so you can see what you are holding and what you would be holding before you spend the level.

The real decision is deepen or widen. The same mark again can go deeper on a chamber it already occupies, feeding a two-chamber fusion, or take a second chamber and pay you a hand. One card, two directions, and you cannot have both.

HIRE WHAT YOU CAN AFFORD

A peddler's wagon rolls onto the field. The silver you pick off the ground buys laudanum, a full cylinder, a blessed nail — or a hand for hire. The Gambler fires fast and hits light. The Widow takes two seconds a shot and rarely misses. The Sawbones stitches you up where he stands. The Preacher reads over them until they give ground.

They walk where you walk, they do one thing each, and anything that touches them is killing them. They do not come back.

FIVE GROUNDS, AND EACH ONE BREAKS A HABIT

  • Boot Hill — the burying ground, and what is under it.
  • Perdition Flats — main street, and nobody on it.
  • The Railyard — you cannot back away at speed over ballast and sleepers.
  • The Salt Flats — no cover for nine miles, and a crosswind pulls every shot.
  • The Deep Mine — you see forty metres, the muzzle flash is your lamp, and the roof comes down: dust first, then the stone.

SIX WHO CAN WALK OUT THERE

The steady Mortician, the three-chamber Sawbones, the twelve-chamber Preacher, the charm-laden Widow, the ever-shuffling Gambler, and the Revenant who cannot be healed but takes another life off every boss.

THIRTEEN NIGHTS, AND SOMETHING AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SHAFT

A story campaign across three acts. Walk a funeral wagon home while the road ahead is held against you. Empty grave-pits that wake when you step into them. Run the town's ledger to the far fence with everything between you and it. Put down the Hanging Judge, cut down the Hanging Tree, and meet the Pale Rider on open ground with four waves of his own dead between you.

The mortician grows between the nights, in the Undertaker's Book — so a night is always six chambers and a steady hand. Finish all thirteen and ride them again at a harder tier; beating a night above your best pays its pages over.

AND THEN THE ENDLESS NIGHTS

Three survivor modes underneath the story: the fixed fifteen-minute night, the Long Night that never ends, and a daily grave on a seed everyone shares.

WOODCUT AND LAMPLIGHT

Every mark in the game is drawn, not painted — hatched ink on aged paper, one colour of brass, and a lot of dark.

WHAT IS IN IT

  • 13 authored nights across three acts, with 114 scripted scenes and a 19-beat epilogue
  • 5 grounds, each with a rule that changes how you play rather than how it looks
  • 6 characters whose chamber counts and core rules rewrite the run
  • 12 engravings and 10 two-chamber fusions, plus 10 gunsmith upgrades and 14 charms
  • 6 named bosses, 15 kinds of dead, and a 21-entry bestiary that fills as you meet them
  • 4 difficulty tiers, in the story as well as the survivor modes
  • 24 contracts and 10 stackable wagers that break a mechanic on purpose for better pay
  • 42 collection entries and 22 achievements
  • Adjustable gore, screen shake, flick sensitivity, and independent master, music and effects volume

You buried them once. Do the job properly this time.

Skeleton Crew: Castle Heist is a 1–4 player co-op game about a group of small skeletons sneaking into dangerous medieval castles, completing objectives, dealing with guards, and trying to make it out alive... or at least with enough bones to put themselves back together. 💀🏰

Explore castles filled with guards, valuable objects, obstacles, and unexpected situations. Depending on the mission, your crew may need to find and extract an object, deliver an item to a specific location, explore part of the castle, complete an objective, or survive the chaos created along the way.

⚙️ PHYSICS-BASED CHAOS

The game is built around physics and interaction with the environment.

Objects have weight and momentum. Heavy objects are difficult to carry, narrow passages can create problems, and even a small collision can completely change the situation.

A simple plan can turn into complete chaos within seconds.

🦴 LIMB LOSS

Skeletons do not use a traditional health system.

Attacks from guards can knock off individual limbs, and losing an arm or leg changes the way you move and interact with the environment.

Detached limbs remain in the world, allowing other players to pick them up and help their teammates put themselves back together.

Losing part of your body does not necessarily mean the raid is over.

🤝 CO-OP FOR 1–4 PLAYERS

Every player is part of the crew.

Some objectives are easier, or even impossible, to complete alone. Carry heavy objects, distract guards, explore the castle, and help teammates who have lost their limbs.

Communicate, divide responsibilities, and work together to improve your chances of escaping.

🏰 DIFFERENT RAIDS

The castle is made up of rooms that are procedurally assembled into different combinations.

Room layouts, routes, obstacles, guard placement, and other elements can change between raids, so you cannot simply memorize one route and repeat it every time.

Objectives can also vary from one mission to another.

🛡️ GUARDS AND PANIC

The castle is protected by different types of enemies.

The Hunter tracks skeletons and reacts to their actions.
The Executioner is a dangerous melee opponent.
The Sorcerer uses magic to interfere with the crew.

Guards can detect players, pursue them, and knock off their limbs.

Noise, destruction, and detection can also increase the Panic level, gradually making the situation more dangerous and harder to control. 🚨

🔮 THE NECROMANCER'S LOBBY

Between raids, the crew returns to the Necromancer's underground crypt.

This serves as the team's base for preparing for the next raid, restoring skeletons, interacting with the game's systems, and entering the castle again through the portal.

Enter the castle. Complete the objective. Help your crew. Escape.

It all starts with a click. Tap the notebook page to mine resources and earn gold. Simple, satisfying and just the beginning.

Spend your hard-earned points to unlock new abilities in the skill tree. Each upgrade opens new paths, new possibilities and new ways to play. Plan your build wisely there's always something worth unlocking next.

Open the notebook and draw your creature by hand. Lines, shapes, whatever feels right once you're done, it comes to life and joins your kingdom ready to work.

Complete missions and put your creatures to the test. Send them into battle and watch your hand-drawn army take on whatever the notebook throws at them. Win, earn rewards and keep growing.

Ski Lines is a minimalist strategy simulation game about designing a ski resort map.

Draw ski runs, build lifts, and connect mountain landmarks as new points of interest appear across the slopes. Every day, more skiers arrive, new destinations open, and your resort becomes harder to keep flowing.

Your goal is simple: keep skiers moving.

Start with a small mountain and a handful of resources. Connect stations, summits, viewpoints, restaurants, refuges, and rescue points with the right mix of pistes and lifts. Easy runs are flexible, harder runs are more demanding, and every new connection changes the shape of your network.

But the mountain is not just a blank canvas. Snow cannons let you expand the skiable area, while tree clearing allows you to open new routes through the forest. Upgrade your lifts, improve your tools, and choose carefully where to invest your limited resources.

As the days pass, the resort grows busier. New points of interest appear, skiers demand better routes, and bottlenecks begin to form. Redesign your network, extend the domain, and adapt before the slopes become overwhelmed.

Key Features

  • Draw ski pistes directly on a stylized trail map.

  • Build lifts to bring skiers back up the mountain.

  • Connect stations, summits, restaurants, refuges, viewpoints, and more.

  • Use snow cannons to expand the skiable area.

  • Clear trees to open new routes through forests.

  • Upgrade lifts, snow cannons, and other tools as your resort grows.

  • Manage limited resources and choose your expansions wisely.

  • Adapt your network as new points of interest appear each day.

  • Play across famous ski regions inspired by resorts around the world.

  • Enjoy replayable runs with roguelike progression and evolving mountain layouts.

  • Level editor & Community maps

Get down the mountain. When it goes wrong, something comes to get you, and it is never the same thing twice.

EVERY WIPEOUT SUMMONS SOMETHING RIDICULOUS

Most games punish a crash. This one answers it. Go down hard and the mountain sends help, and help is having a strange day. A giant hand reaching all the way down into the chasm. A marching band nobody asked for. You do not pick which one arrives. That is the point. Players compare notes about which ones they have seen, and there are ones you have not seen yet.

DISTANCE IS THE GOAL. FLOW IS THE REASON TO TAKE THE BAD LINE.

Each level gives you a target and a rescue line to clear. Then the hill starts offering reasons to leave your line. Coins where you should not be. An animal that needs help. A UFO with a tractor beam and a countdown, which a thrown pole can settle if your timing is right. Keep it clean and the flow multiplier climbs. Take the greedy line and it can climb faster, right up until it does not.

FOUR SKIERS. ONE OF THEM IS NOT A PERSON.

Each rider handles differently, and the Yeti has to be earned. He is heavier, he carries a first aid kit, and he clears things the others should not attempt.

EASY MODE IS NOT THE SAME HILL MADE SLOWER.

It is a hill built so a kid and the person who taught them can both finish a run and mean it.

One person makes this game. A bug report gets read by the person who wrote the bug, and a good idea can be in the next build.

Every Battle Makes You Stronger

Step into the ultimate progression loop. In Skillpoint Warrior, your potential is limitless. Whether you are grinding through hordes of enemies or facing bosses, every swing of your weapon brings you closer to your next major power spike.

Core Features:

  • Forge Your Build: Defeat enemies to harvest valuable Skill Points. Invest them into stats like Strength, Vitality, and Agility.

  • Loot & Equip: Base stats are just the beginning. Discover and equip powerful armor, weapons, and accessories that multiply your power.

  • Conquer Diverse Worlds: Journey through a variety of unique realms, each packed with increasingly challenging enemies and new tiers of loot.
